'''Nemanja Bjelica''' ({{Langx|sr|Немања Бјелица}}, {{IPA|sr|němaɲa bjělitsa|pron}}; born 9 May 1988)<ref name="Kurir"/> is a Serbian executive and former professional [[basketball]] player who most recently became sporting director for [[Bahçeşehir Koleji S.K.|Bahçeşehir Koleji]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL). He represented the senior [[Serbia national basketball team|Serbian national team]] in international competition. Bjelica was an [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-Euroleague First Team]] selection as well as the [[Euroleague MVP]] in [[2014–15 Euroleague|2015]]. Bjelica started his NBA career as a 27-year-old rookie when he signed in 2015 and played for the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] for three seasons before signing with the [[Sacramento Kings]] in the 2018 offseason. In 2021, he was traded to the [[Miami Heat]] before signing with the [[Golden State Warriors]] during the offseason. With the Warriors, he won an [[List of NBA champions|NBA championship]] in 2022.

==Club career==
===Early career (2007–2010)===
[[Image:Bjelica Nemanja cropped.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Bjelica playing for [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]] ]]
Bjelica began playing basketball at Aca Janjić basketball school, before joining the [[youth system]] of [[KK Partizan]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bjelica za Mondo: Imam glavu plejmejkera|url=http://mondo.rs/a117793/Sport/Kosarka/Bjelica-za-MONDO-Imam-glavu-plejmejkera.html|access-date=27 December 2018|website=mondo.rs|date=20 November 2008|language=sr}}</ref> He began his professional career in the 2007–08 season with the [[Traiskirchen Lions|Arkadia Traiskirchen Lions]] of the [[Österreichische Basketball Bundesliga|Austrian League]], earning 8.5 points in 26 matches on average.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Nemanja Bjelica|url=https://www.basketballliga.at/spieler?player_id=18600|access-date=27 December 2018|website=Basketball Liga|language=de|archive-date=28 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181228034917/https://www.basketballliga.at/spieler?player_id=18600 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

After one season abroad, Bjelica returned to the Serbian team [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]] and spent two successful seasons there under [[head coach]] [[Svetislav Pešić]]. During the 2008–09 season, he made breakthroughs, and earned a place in the first lineup. He was particularly noted for his performance during the [[ULEB Cup|EuroCup]], for his outside shooting. Later in his career, Bjelica cited coach Pešić as one of the main reasons for his improvement as a player.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Nemanja Bjelica za Telegraf: Da nije bilo Pešića, ostao bih prosečno krilo (Video)|url=http://www.telegraf.rs/sport/481742-nemanja-bjelica-za-telegraf-da-nije-bilo-pesica-ostao-bih-prosecno-krilo-video |access-date=14 July 2015 |website=Telegraf.rs|date=6 January 2013 |language=sr}}</ref> Coach Pešić trusted Bjelica with the ball, and gave the 6"10 Bjelica a primary ball handler role on several occasions, which helped to develop Bjelica as a playmaker.{{Citation needed|date=June 2026}} Bjelica was drafted by the [[Washington Wizards]] with the 35th pick of the [[2010 NBA draft]]. His draft rights were then traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/Minnesota_Acquires_Draft_Rights_to_Lazar_Hayward_2010_06_25.html|url-status=dead|title=Minnesota Acquires Draft Rights to Lazar Hayward|publisher=NBA|date=25 June 2010|access-date=17 October 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110622053046/https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/minnesota_acquires_draft_rights_to_lazar_hayward_2010_06_25.html|archive-date=22 June 2011}}</ref>

In August 2010, Bjelica signed a five-year contract with Spanish club [[Saski Baskonia]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Caja Laboral lands Nemanja Bjelica |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/74402/caja-laboral-lands-nemanja-bjelica|url-status=dead|access-date=18 May 2015|website=Euroleague.net|date=2 August 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150519141245/http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/74402/caja-laboral-lands-nemanja-bjelica|archive-date=19 May 2015}}</ref>

===Fenerbahçe (2013–2015)===
On 22 July 2013, Bjelica signed a three-year contract with the Turkish club [[Fenerbahçe Ülker]], which was led by one of Europe's great coaches, [[Željko Obradović]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Fenerbahce will sign Nemanja Bjelica to a three-year deal |url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/turkey/59982/fenerbahce-will-sign-nemanja-bjelica-to-a-three-year-deal.html |publisher=Sportando.net |access-date=23 July 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Bjelica kod Obradovića u Feneru |url=http://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2013&mm=07&dd=22&nav_id=735008 |website=[[B92]]|date=22 July 2013 |access-date=23 July 2013|language=sr}}</ref> He cited Obradović as the main reason why he didn't go to the [[NBA]] instead.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Bjelica: Željko Obradović i ja, nestvarno! |url=http://www.novosti.rs/vesti/sport.295.html%3A445541-Bjelica-Zeljko-Obradovic-i-ja-nestvarno |access-date=30 April 2015|newspaper=[[Večernje novosti]]|date=23 July 2013|language=sr}}</ref> In the 2013–14 season, he immediately became one of the key players of Fenerbahçe Ülker, earning career highs of 10.4 points, 6.1 rebounds, 2.2 assists, and 1.6 steals per game over 24 EuroLeague games on average.

The following season, on 30 March 2015, Bjelica was named [[EuroLeague MVP of the Month]] for March, his first such monthly award in his career. Over four matches played in March, he earned 15 points, 9 rebounds, 3 assists, and 1 block per match on average.<ref>{{cite news |title=bwin MVP for March: Nemanja Bjelica, Fenerbahce Ulker Istanbul |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/5up9fmj3a5ncsf47/bwin-mvp-for-march-nemanja-bjelica-fenerbahce-ulker-istanbul|url-status=dead|website=Euroleague|date=8 May 2015|access-date=30 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304135925/http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/5xtj7vjfuokfw7g8|archive-date=4 March 2016}}</ref> In May 2015, he was chosen to the [[All-EuroLeague Team|All-EuroLeague First Team]], for his performances over the season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=All-Euroleague First and Second Teams announced |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/5xtj7vjfuokfw7g8 |access-date=8 May 2015|website=Euroleague}}</ref> Eventually, Bjelica was named [[EuroLeague MVP]] of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2014-15 bwin MVP: Nemanja Bjelica, Fenerbahce Ulker Istanbul |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/5ycw47oqktncu4e3 |access-date=14 May 2015|website=Euroleague|date=14 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305004741/http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/5ycw47oqktncu4e3|archive-date=5 March 2016}}</ref> Fenerbahçe also advanced to the [[2015 Euroleague Final Four|EuroLeague Final Four]] for the first time in the team's history.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Fenerbahce for the first time in the Final Four|url=http://www.eurohoops.net/2015/04/league-action/87436/ |access-date=15 May 2015|website=Eurohoops|date=20 April 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150518101508/http://www.eurohoops.net/2015/04/league-action/87436/|archive-date=18 May 2015}}</ref> However, on 15 May, they lost in the semifinal against [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]], by a score of 87–96.<ref>{{cite news |title=Real Madrid heads to third straight final after beating Fenerbahce |url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=248&seasoncode=E2014#!report |access-date=15 May 2015 |website=EuroBasket|date=15 May 2015}}</ref> Eventually, Fenerbahçe finished fourth place after losing in the third-place play-off against [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]], by a score of 80–86.<ref>{{cite news |title=CSKA Moscow beats Fenerbahce in third-place game |url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=250&seasoncode=E2014#!report|url-status=dead|access-date=18 May 2015|website=Euroleague|date=17 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160130153519/http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=250&seasoncode=E2014#!report#!report|archive-date=30 January 2016}}</ref> Bjelica had his best season since he signed for the club, earning a career-high 12.1 points, 8.5 rebounds, 1.9 assists, and 1.3 steals on average per match. However, Fenerbahçe, finished the season without winning any trophy, after also losing in the semi-final series of the [[2014–15 Turkish Basketball League|Turkish League]] championship, againstthe eventual league champions [[Karşıyaka Basket|Pınar Karşıyaka]].{{Citation needed|date=June 2026}} On 1 July, Bjelica ended his contract with Fenerbahçe to play in the [[NBA]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Fenerbahce opts out of Nemanja Bjelica's contract |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/166463/fenerbahce-opts-out-of-nemanja-bjelica-s-contract.html|url-status=dead|access-date=1 July 2015|website=Sportando|date=1 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304115818/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/166463/fenerbahce-opts-out-of-nemanja-bjelica-s-contract.html|archive-date=4 March 2016}}</ref>

=== Minnesota Timberwolves (2015–2018) ===
On 14 July 2015, Bjelica signed with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-sign-reigning-euroleague-most-valuable-player-nemanja-bjelica |title=Timberwolves Sign Reigning Euroleague Most Valuable Player Nemanja Bjelica|publisher=NBA|date=14 July 2015 |access-date=14 July 2015}}</ref> He made his debut for the Timberwolves in their season opener on 28 October, recording eight points and five rebounds in a 112–111 victory against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/MINLAL/gameinfo.html |title=Wolves edge Lakers 112-111 in first game since Flip's death|publisher=NBA|date=28 October 2015 |access-date=29 October 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151026213514/http://www.nba.com/games/20151028/MINLAL/gameinfo.html |archive-date=26 October 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref> On 7 November, Bjelica had a season-best game with 17 points, 11 rebounds, five assists, one steal and one block against the [[Chicago Bulls]]. On 7 April 2016, he scored a season-high 18 points against the [[Sacramento Kings]]. Four days later, he recorded 11 points and a season-high 14 rebounds against the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/bjeline01/gamelog/2016/ |title=Nemanja Bjelica 2015-16 Game Log|website=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=14 November 2016}}</ref>

On 13 November 2016, Bjelica made his first career start and scored a career-high 24 points in a 125–99 victory against the Los Angeles Lakers.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899592 |title=Wiggins scores 47 to lead Timberwolves over Lakers, 125-99|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=13 November 2016 |access-date=14 November 2016}}</ref> On 16 March 2017, he was ruled out for the rest of the 2016–17 season due to a left foot injury.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/nemanja-bjelica-injury-update-0 |title=Nemanja Bjelica Injury Update|publisher=NBA|date=16 March 2017 |access-date=16 March 2017}}</ref> He underwent surgery five days later to repair a fractured navicular bone in his left foot.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/nemanja-bjelica-injury-update-1 |title=Nemanja Bjelica Injury Update|date=21 March 2017 |access-date=21 March 2017}}</ref> Bjelica missed 15 matches, spanning November and December of the 2017–18 season with a sprained left foot.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974449 |title=Timberwolves beat Lakers 121-104 for first Christmas win|publisher=ESPN|date=25 December 2017 |access-date=26 December 2017}}</ref> On 8 March 2018, he scored a career-high 30 points on 11-for-16 shooting, including 6 for 9 from 3-point range, in a 117–109 loss to the [[Boston Celtics]]. He also had 12 rebounds to record his first 20–10 game in the NBA.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975720 |title=Irving returns to carry Celtics past Timberwolves 117-109|publisher=ESPN|date=8 March 2018 |access-date=8 March 2018}}</ref>

=== Sacramento Kings and Miami Heat (2018–2021) ===
On 21 July 2018, just days after backing out of a contract with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] with the intention of returning to Europe, Bjelica signed a three-year, $20.5 million contract with the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/king-sign-nemanja-bjelica |title=Kings Sign Nemanja Bjelica|publisher=ESPN|date=21 July 2018 |access-date=21 July 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/24153933/nemanja-bjelica-sacramento-kings-agree-3-year-deal |title=Nemanja Bjelica staying in the U.S. after all, reaches deal with Kings|publisher=ESPN|date=21 July 2018 |access-date=21 July 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/24121270/nemanja-bjelica-sign-philadelphia-76ers-plans-stay-europe |title=Nemanja Bjelica won't sign with 76ers, plans to stay in Europe|publisher=ESPN|date=17 July 2018 |access-date=21 July 2018}} On 9 December 2019, Bjelica drilled a buzzer beating 3-pointer to lift the Kings to a road 119-118 victory against the [[Houston Rockets]],. On 13 January 2020, he set career highs with 34 points and 8 3-pointers in a 114-112 loss to the [[Orlando Magic]].</ref> On 25 March 2021, Bjelica was traded to the [[Miami Heat]] in exchange for [[Maurice Harkless]] and [[Chris Silva]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=HEAT Acquire Nemanja Bjelica|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-acquire-nemanja-bjelica-032521|publisher=NBA|date=25 March 2021}}</ref>

=== Golden State Warriors (2021–2022) ===
On 6 August 2021, Bjelica signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/nemanja-bjelica-20210806 |title=Warriors Sign Free Agent Forward Nemanja Bjelica |work=NBA.com |date=6 August 2021}}</ref> He made his debut for the Warriors in their season opener on 19 October 2021, recording a [[double-double]] off the bench with 15 points and 11 rebounds in a 121–114 victory against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Curry, Warriors stun James, Lakers 121-114 in opener |url=https://www.nba.com/game/gsw-vs-lal-0022100002 |website=NBA|date=19 October 2021|access-date=20 October 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Skoro savršeno veče Nemanje Bjelice: Dabl-dablom režirao preokret za pobedu u Gradu anđela |url=https://mozzartsport.com/kosarka/vesti/skoro-savrseno-vece-nemanje-bjelice-dabl-dablom-rezirao-preokret-za-pobedu-u-gradu-anela-video/401647 |website=mozzartsport.com |access-date=20 October 2021}}</ref> He became the first player to post a double-double off the bench in his Warriors debut since [[Sam Williams (basketball, born 1959)|Sam Williams]] (16 points, 12 rebounds) on 30 October 1981 at [[Denver]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Bjelica zabeležio debi kakav nije viđen 40 godina |url=https://mozzartsport.com/kosarka/vesti/bjelica-zabelezio-debi-kakav-nije-vien-40-godina/401659 |website=Mozzart Sport|date=20 October 2021|access-date=29 June 2026|language=sr}}</ref> During the [[2022 NBA Finals]], Bjelica held [[Boston Celtics|Celtics]] star [[Jayson Tatum]] to 0-6 shooting and 4 turnovers en route to his first NBA championship.<ref>{{Cite tweet |title=Register |url-access=limited |user=statmuse |number=1536524724926197760 |url=https://mobile.twitter.com/statmuse/status/1536524724926197760 |access-date=17 June 2022}}</ref> He became the fourth [[List of Serbian NBA players|NBA player from Serbia]] who won the championship, joining [[Darko Miličić]], [[Peja Stojaković]], and [[Ognjen Kuzmić]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Nemanja Bjelica četvrti Srbin sa NBA prstenom |url=https://mozzartsport.com/kosarka/vesti/nemanja-bjelica-cetvrti-srbin-sa-nba-prstenom/422892 |website=Mozzart Sport|date=17 June 2022|access-date=29 June 2026}}</ref>

===Later career and retirement (2022–2024)===
On 9 August 2022, Bjelica re-signed for [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe]] on a two-year contract, where he was named the [[EuroLeague MVP]] of the [[2014–15 Euroleague|2014-15]] season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Fenerbahçe Beko, Nemanja Bjelica Transferini Resmen Açıkladı! |trans-title=Fenerbahçe officially announced Nemanja Bjelica's transfer|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/tr/euroleague-tr/1370217/bomba-fenerbahce-beko-nemanja-bjelica-transferini-resmen-acikladi/|website=Eurohoops|date=9 August 2022|access-date=29 June 2026|language=tr}}</ref> Upon missing much of the season due to a calf injury, Bjelica finally made his season debut on 3 March 2023.{{Clarify|date=June 2026}}{{Citation needed|date=June 2026}} On 12 September 2023, he was released by Fenerbahçe.<ref name=eurohoops>{{Cite web |last=Askounis |first=Johnny |date=12 September 2023 |title=Nemanja Bjelica parts ways with Fenerbahce and reunites with Crvena Zvezda |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1552779/fenerbahce-releases-nemanja-bjelica-euroleague/|website=Eurohoops|access-date=28 June 2026}}</ref> Hours after being released by Fenerbahçe, he returned to Serbia, signed a contract with Crvena zvezda.<ref name=eurohoops/> On 9 October 2023, after getting caught in a fight with [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]] head coach [[Duško Ivanović]], Bjelica allegedly has parted ways with his hometown club.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Nemanja Bjelica otisao iz Crvene zvezde zbog sukoba sa Duskom Ivanovicem|url=https://www.kurir.rs/sport/kosarka/4262720/nemanja-bjelica-otisao-iz-crvene-zvezde-zbog-sukoba-sa-duskom-ivanovicem|website=[[Kurir]]|date=10 October 2023|access-date=29 June 2026|language=sr}}</ref> On 23 March 2024, Bjelica officially announced his retirement from professional basketball.<ref>{{cite web|first=Johnny|last=Askounis|title=Nemanja Bjelica calls it a day: "Thank you basketball"|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1649010/nemanja-bjelica-retires-euroleague-nba-fiba/|website=EuroHoops.net|date=23 March 2024|access-date=29 June 2026}}</ref>

==National team career==
[[File:Nemanja-bjelica-universiade-2009-beograd-atipiks.jpg|thumb|250px|right|Bjelica taking on Israel as part of the gold medal-winning [[Serbian men's university basketball team|Serbian university team]] at the [[Basketball at the 2009 Summer Universiade – Men|2009 Summer Universiade]] in Belgrade.]]
Bjelica was a member of the [[Serbia men's national basketball team|Serbia national basketball team]] at the [[EuroBasket 2015]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ambitious Serbia Unveil Powerful 12-man Squad|url=http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_xUMkR0x,HeIT9w-vv9Ob00.articleMode_on.html |access-date=3 September 2015|website=Eurobasket 2015|date=2 September 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150905064710/http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_xUMkR0x,HeIT9w-vv9Ob00.articleMode_on.html |archive-date=5 September 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref> In Serbia's opening match, an 80–70 victory against [[Spain national basketball team|Spain]], he was Serbia's key player, posting 24 points, 10 rebounds, and 4 assists. The following day, he made a game-winning shot against [[Germany national basketball team|Germany]]. In the last match of the group phase, he scored 19 points, grabbed 8 rebounds, and had four assists against [[Italy national basketball team|Italy]]. Serbia dominated in the tournament's toughest group, [[EuroBasket 2015 Group B|Group B]], with a 5–0 record, and then eliminated [[Finland national basketball team|Finland]] and the [[Czech Republic national basketball team|Czech Republic]] in the round of 16 and quarterfinal games, respectively. However, they were stopped in the semifinal game by [[Lithuania men's national basketball team|Lithuania]], by a score of 67–64,<ref>{{cite news |title=Lithuania End Serbia Streak, Return to the Final|url=http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/gameID_11664-76-A-1.html |access-date=20 September 2015 |website=Eurobasket 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150919004022/http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/gameID_11664-76-A-1.html |archive-date=19 September 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref> and eventually lost against the host team, [[France national basketball team|France]], in the bronze-medal game, by a score of 81–68.<ref>{{cite news |title=France Reward Home Support with Bronze|url=http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_XCBBt0,vHwcDLI3DN0sTU1.articleMode_on.html |access-date=20 September 2015 |work=eurobasket2015.org |date=20 September 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150922234352/http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.coid_XCBBt0,vHwcDLI3DN0sTU1.articleMode_on.html |archive-date=22 September 2015 |url-status=usurped}}</ref> Being one of the team's leaders, along with [[Miloš Teodosić]] and [[Miroslav Raduljica]], Bjelica earned 13.9 points, 6.6 rebounds, and 2.7 assists per match on average, on 56.1% shooting from the field and 37.5% shooting from behind the three-point line.<ref>{{cite web |title=Player profile: Nemanja Bjelica |url=http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.teamID_96799.playerID_61824.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20150920164635/http://www.eurobasket2015.org/en/compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2015.roundID_9322.teamID_96799.playerID_61824.html |url-status=dead|archive-date=20 September 2015 |website=eurobasket2015.org |publisher=FIBA Europe |access-date=20 September 2015}}</ref>

At the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup]], the national team of Serbia was dubbed as favorite to win the trophy,<ref>{{Cite web|first=Igor|last=Curkovic|title=FIBA Basketball World Cup Power Rankings, Volume 3 |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2019/news/fiba-basketball-world-cup-power-rankings-volume-3 |access-date=14 September 2019|publisher=FIBA|date=28 August 2019}}</ref> but was eventually upset in the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup final round|quarterfinals]] by [[Argentina national basketball team|Argentina]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Argentina upsets Olympic silver medalist Serbia in FIBA World Cup quarterfinals |url=https://olympics.nbcsports.com/2019/09/10/argentina-serbia-fiba-world-cup/ |access-date=14 September 2019 |website=NBC Sports|date=10 September 2019}}</ref> With wins over the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States]] and [[Czech Republic national basketball team|Czech Republic]], it finished in fifth place.<ref>{{cite news |title=Serbia defeats USA in FIBA World Cup consolation round play |url=https://www.nba.com/article/2019/09/12/fiba-world-cup-usa-serbia-game-recap |access-date=14 September 2019|publisher=NBA|date=12 September 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Bogdanović ponovo briljirao – Srbiji peto mesto u Kini |url=https://www.b92.net/sport/kina2019/vesti.php?nav_id=1591176|website=B92|access-date=14 September 2019 |date=14 September 2019 |language=sr}}</ref> Bjelica's statistics suggest he was the third-best player on the team behind [[Bogdan Bogdanović (basketball)|Bogdanović]] and [[Nikola Jokić|Jokić]], earning 10.7 points, 4.7 rebounds and 2.7 assists over seven matches in average, while shooting 42.9% from the field.

==Post-playing career==
In April 2024, [[Bahçeşehir Koleji S.K.|Bahçeşehir Koleji]] appointed Bjelica as the club's new head of basketball operations for the 2024–25 season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Nemanja Bjelica preuzima direktorsku fotelju Bahčešehira: Turski klub puno očekuje od "profesora"|url=https://www.tvarenasport.com/kosarka/aba-liga/25855/nemanja-bjelica-novi-sportski-direktor-bahcesehira/news|website=Arena Sport|date=21 April 2024|access-date=29 June 2026|language=sr}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Bjelica was brought up in the [[New Belgrade]] [[Blokovi|Blocks]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sedam Kratkij Pitanja na Nemanju Bjelicu|url=http://www.koledz-beograd.edu.rs/bjelica_jun2013.html |access-date=17 July 2015 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304044718/http://www.koledz-beograd.edu.rs/bjelica_jun2013.html |url-status=dead}}</ref> He married in June 2012 and has two children.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Crkveno venčanje Mirjane i Nemanje Bjelice|url=http://www.novosti.rs/vesti/scena.147.html:385360-Crkveno-vencanje-Mirjane-i-Nemanje-Bjelice|access-date=27 January 2015|newspaper=Večernje novosti|date=22 June 2012|language=sr}}</ref><ref name="The New York Times">{{Cite news|first=Jon|last=Krawczynski|title=How Nemanja Bjelica and family found footing in a new league and a new land|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/158257/2017/11/17/nemanja-bjelica-mirjana-minnesota-timberwolves-nba-serbia/|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=17 November 2017|access-date=29 June 2026}}</ref> Apart from his native Serbian, Bjelica speaks English fluently.<ref name="The New York Times"/>

On 5 February 2024, Bjelica was threatened with scissors in [[Belgrade, Serbia]]. In the incident, the man told Bjelica: "I would take your family, your children, your wife, and you", and also threatened to stab him with the scissors.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Nemanja Bjelica threatened with scissors: "I'll take your family"|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1624429/nemanja-bjelica/|access-date=8 February 2024|website=Eurohoops|date=5 February 2024}}</ref>
